title: The Pulse, Monday 19 October 2026
tldr: DeepSeek shipped V4.1 Flash 1017 with vision and 1M context for 15¢/60¢ per million tokens. Claude Code's team wrote about how they do code review when the agent writes 90% of the code. The weekend brought three days' worth of agentic memory papers, CLI benchmarks, and safety research.

models.title: DeepSeek: DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 1017
models.summary: DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 1017 is the October 17 snapshot of DeepSeek's sparse mixture-of-experts model, now with vision (text+image->text), 1M context, and improved reasoning.
models.why: Matches Claude 3.7 performance on SWE-bench Verified at a tenth of the cost; the whole Pipeline stack runs through OpenRouter so this is immediately available for all our agentic call grading and retrieval workflows.

models.title: Elorian: Glimpse
models.summary: Glimpse is a visual reasoning model from Elorian built for physical-world understanding; it handles images and video (text+image+video->text) with 262K context.
models.why: Video understanding for EverRaise's call recordings and Life International's training materials; the multimodal reasoning could help Meno's bill-tracking agents verify document changes across video briefings.

models.title: Reflection: Beam 1.0 501B A23B
models.summary: Beam 1.0 is Reflection's open-weight reasoning model for coding and long-horizon agentic workflows, 501B total with 23B active per token and 1M context.
models.why: Built specifically for agentic coding workflows; worth testing on Botterfly's skill authoring and wehshi review panel tasks where reasoning depth matters more than raw speed.

models.title: NVIDIA Nemotron Labs Dory1.0 4B
models.summary: Dory1.0 is a 4B conversational model from NVIDIA's Nemotron Labs, released in BF16, MXFP8, NVFP4, and GGUF quantizations.
models.why: Small enough to run on-device for SalesKick's call grading pilots on RTX laptops; the GGUF release means we can eval it in llama.cpp before committing to fine-tuning.

research.title: AuditKIT: A Unified Evaluation Spine for Benchmarking, Judging, and Comparing Large Language Models and Agentic Systems
research.summary: AuditKIT combines benchmark accuracy, judge-based assessment, runtime performance, tool-use behavior, and retrieval quality into one evaluation framework for LLM agents.
research.why: Exactly what we need for systematic comparison of wehshi review models and EverRaise's Vapi-based voice agents; the unified trace format could feed our Langfuse observability stack.

research.title: MetaCurate: Evolving Curation Filters for High-Quality Agentic Coding Data
research.summary: MetaCurate learns to filter agentic coding trajectories by distinguishing useful intermediate steps from noise, even in failed runs.
research.why: Our wehshi panel and Claude Code sessions generate thousands of trajectories; this could help us curate the keepers for fine-tuning Botterfly's skill authoring and code review behavior.

research.title: SAFE-Mem: Secure Agentic Memory with Fine-Grained Authority and Governance-Aware Retrieval
research.summary: SAFE-Mem prevents untrusted claims in LLM agent memory from being treated as authorized preferences or permissions.
research.why: Hermes Agent's Mnemosyne memory lets agents store facts from external sources; this addresses the exact security gap we saw when a Pipeline client's scraped data was mistaken for a preference.

research.title: Ignored, Not Refused: What Low Prompt-Injection Success Rates Hide in Small Tool-Using Agents
research.summary: Audit of 33K trajectories shows that prompt-injection defenses work by ignoring the attack, but the agent still exposes the injected content through other tool calls.
research.why: Every Pipeline voice agent reads untrusted caller input and calls tools; if our defense is silent ignoring, the attack still leaks through context — this tells us what to test.

research.title: From Relevant Memories to Sufficient Evidence: Rethinking Memory Utilization in LLM Agents
research.summary: Retrieving relevant memories doesn't guarantee sufficient evidence for reasoning; essential information stays fragmented across memory records, obscured by abstraction.
research.why: Mnemosyne's hybrid recall pulls memories by similarity, but this shows why our agents still miss facts — relevance ≠ sufficiency; the paper's evidence-chaining method could improve Botterfly's decision recall.

releases.title: LangChain Core 1.6.12
releases.summary: Fixes extra propagation on content-block-start events.
releases.why: We use LangChain Core across SalesKick's nurturing agents; the content-block-start fix unblocks streaming for Mackinac's research workflows where we show partial results.

releases.title: Langfuse 4.63.0
releases.summary: Ships skill management as a public v4 preview, AI gateway codex-model routing, and annotation queue UX improvements.
releases.why: We've been waiting for public skill management to systematize Botterfly's procedural memory; the codex-model routing lets us send slugless models to the OpenAI connection without manual mapping.

releases.title: Langfuse 4.62.0
releases.summary: Adds AI gateway per-connection model controls, request limit raised to 16 MiB, and OTEL third-party span metadata decoding.
releases.why: The 16 MiB request limit unblocks EverRaise's longer call transcripts through the gateway; per-connection model controls let us route client-specific provider credentials cleanly.

releases.title: Langfuse 4.61.0
releases.summary: Adds dedicated skills tab on traces, AI gateway connection-based routing, and skill usage metrics.
releases.why: Skills-on-traces visibility means we can finally see which Botterfly skills fired for each wehshi panel run; the metrics will show which skills are dead weight.

hackernews.title: Claude reveals ECDSA curve origins
hackernews.summary: Anthropic used Claude to trace the provenance of the ECDSA P-256 curve constants back to deliberate parameter choices in 1991 NIST research, not unexplained magic numbers.
hackernews.why: Shows a reasoning model can reconstruct cryptographic design decisions from decades-old papers; the same investigative approach could help us audit black-box third-party SDKs in client stacks.

hackernews.title: How the Claude Code team does code review
hackernews.summary: Claude Code writes 90% of its own code; the team shifted code review from line-by-line diffs to automated verification, self-fixing agents, and human focus on design decisions only.
hackernews.why: Exactly the problem we're solving with wehshi: when agents write faster than we can review, verification becomes the bottleneck — their playbook (gate on tests, autofix lints, verify claims) directly informs our PR review pipeline.

hackernews.title: DeepSeek search and fetch – $0.75 per 1000 successful requests
hackernews.summary: DeepSeek launched a search and fetch API at 75¢ per 1K successful requests; it returns search results as structured JSON for LLM consumption.
hackernews.why: Mackinac's legislative research and EverRaise's donor intelligence both need live web search; at 75¢ per thousand this undercuts our current Serper and Brave bills by 80% — test immediately.

hackernews.title: OpenCode Hacked: User credentials leaked
hackernews.summary: OpenCode disclosed a breach that leaked user credentials; the service was temporarily shut down while the team rotated keys and notified users.
hackernews.why: OpenCode is referenced in our skills and deployment docs; we need to audit any OpenCode integrations across SalesKick and Pipeline for credential exposure and rotate affected keys.

x_posts.title: @ClaudeDevs on performance improvements
x_posts.summary: Claude Code now gzips the conversation before sending it to the model on every turn, making the agent start responding sooner; cloud sessions also start as soon as typing begins.
x_posts.why: Latency matters for interactive agents; we can borrow the gzip-before-send trick for Hermes sessions with long Mnemosyne recall or sprawling skill contexts.

x_posts.title: @fchollet on software engineering in 2026
x_posts.summary: François Chollet observes that there are more software engineers now than in 2025, demand is growing, they work harder than ever, and agents write ~100% of the code.
x_posts.why: Matches what we're seeing: Botterfly and wehshi write the code, but we're busier because the bottleneck moved to design, verification, and integrating what the agents built — no direct use for us yet.

x_posts.title: @NousResearch on Hermes Agent and NVIDIA RTX Spark
x_posts.summary: Hermes Agent is a launch partner for NVIDIA's RTX Spark across the new generation of laptops; users can pick it in the built-in Windows agent setup flow.
x_posts.why: Hermes is our daily driver for Botterfly and all Pipeline work; RTX Spark partnership means clients buying new dev machines get Hermes out of the box — good for adoption, and Linus is impressed.

closing: Python releases: nothing notable in the window. DeepSeek and Claude Code dominated the weekend; expect a lot of teams testing V4.1 Flash this week.
